data.narrative: Completed Module 4 'Postmortems & Blameless Culture' learning about blameless culture, five-whys vs timeline-based postmortem formats, writing a postmortem for order processing failure, identifying 19 blame instances in a flawed postmortem, and rewriting it to blameless version with systemic root causes and system-change action items.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified 19 instances of blame in flawed postmortem and explained why each is problematic
dimension_scores.evidence: blame_heavy_analysis.md contains detailed analysis of blame instances and their impact

dimension_scores.observation: Wrote blameless postmortem with clear systemic root causes, no individual names, investigative tone
dimension_scores.evidence: postmortem_order_failure_fixed.md focuses on systems not people

dimension_scores.observation: Wrote postmortem for engineering audience with focus on systemic analysis, avoiding blame to encourage incident reporting
dimension_scores.evidence: postmortem_order_failure_fixed.md uses roles and systems, not individual names

dimension_scores.observation: Applied five-whys format to drill down to systemic root causes, structured with summary, analysis, root cause, contributing factors, action items, lessons learned
dimension_scores.evidence: postmortem_order_failure_fixed.md has all 6 required sections in logical order

dimension_scores.observation: All action items are system changes with specific owners, deadlines, and definitions of done - no 'be more careful' items
dimension_scores.evidence: postmortem_order_failure_fixed.md has 6 action items all as system changes

strengths: Chose five-whys format with reasoning about drilling to root cause
Wrote postmortem with no individual names in root cause or contributing factors
Identified all blame instances in flawed postmortem (19 total)
Rewrote flawed postmortem to blameless version with systemic analysis and system-change action items
data.recommendation: Continue practicing postmortem writing with focus on organizational change - getting teams to adopt blameless culture is harder than writing good postmortems
